subject: Stock issuance planning: off-cycle board slot & 409A alignment
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Timing for Julie Martin offer + potential off-cycle board slot

Hi Markus / Vivek —

Quick heads-up: Recruiting would like to extend an offer to Julie Martin (senior infra engineer) next week. Compensation team ran the numbers and we can meet her target base and cash bonus, but her equity ask (target 0.25% fully diluted) pushes us up against the Q4 grant pool.

We have two constraints:
- Board is not scheduled again until Jan 12, 2027 (regular calendar).
- Our 409A update is due mid-December (we have a draft from finance attached).

Options we're weighing:
1) Ask for an off-cycle board approval (special consent) next week to allow a Dec 15 grant date that matches the expected 409A price;
2) Issue a conditional offer that pins equity until after the Jan board (risk: candidate may accept elsewhere);
3) Use an interim interim policy (time-vesting mock grant with paperwork to follow) — legal prefers actual board approval.

Could you advise if we should push for a special board tranche? If yes, I can coordinate the board packet and run a short notice with Greenline (seed investor) to see if they’ll sign off remotely. Attaching: Q4-board-proposal-packet.pdf and the 409A summary.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Recruiting | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Timing for Julie Martin offer + potential off-cycle board slot

Laura —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Short answer: yes, push for the off-cycle board slot. Rationale: the candidate is strong and the hit to hiring velocity is higher cost than a one-off board convening. A few asks before I reach out to investors:

- Please shrink the board packet to a one-pager + redlines for the form of grant (we need the exact grant instrument and strike/ISOs vs NSOs details).
- Confirm the target grant date you want — proposed Dec 15 (to line up with expected 409A). If 409A misses, we should have fallback language to reprice or delay grant.
- Work with finance to confirm that the December 409A draft supports the strike price for the proposed grant. If not, we should request a short-notice valuation update; include estimated cost of that in the packet.

I'll draft a short note to Greenline and the independent board members this afternoon asking for a remote consent on Dec 14 or Dec 15. Vivek, if you can confirm budget headroom (one-off grant pool and any reserve), that will help me signal the ask. Marissa — please prepare the HR sign-off language and tax withholding note for the packet.

On the legal side, we want DocuSign-ready grant paperwork if the board approves. Can we include a placeholder from Ava Legal and route for signatures the same day?

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Finance & Operations | Redwood Inference

Markus / Laura —

Greenline has reviewed the packet. We can support a remote written consent for a one-off grant but need:
1) The exact grant instrument (form of option agreement) and strike price;
2) A short memo confirming 409A timing and the expected price range;
3) Confirmation that the grant pool/reserve was approved by prior board action or will be covered by this consent.

We prefer not to do re-pricing post-approval; if the 409A price is uncertain, include a fallback clause that defers issuance until valuation finalization and that the option is effective as of the valuation date. Greenline is OK with a December 15 effective grant date if the 409A provider signs off by Dec 10.

I can be on the consent thread next week. If you prepare a redlined grant instrument, I’ll run comments quickly.

—Emily

Team / Greenline —

Update after coordination with finance and HR: we have a compressed plan and a document set ready for review. Summary of outcomes and next steps:

- Remote consent requested for Tue, Dec 14 at 9:00am PT (deadline for investor responses EOD Dec 13). This will authorize a batch of off-cycle option grants, including Julie Martin.
- Finance confirmed the 409A draft supports the expected price range; valuation firm can finalize by Dec 10 if we greenlight the short-notice update (finance to cover expedited fee, ~USD 4k). See 409A-summary-202612.pdf attached.
- Legal (Greenline counsel) provided required checklist. Marissa, please attach the final redlined Option Agreement and the HR sign-off language when you circulate the consent packet on Monday.
- If remote consent passes, Ava Legal will prepare DocuSign envelopes and we will execute grants with an effective grant date of Dec 15. If the 409A finalizes later, we will include a valuation-effective clause as discussed.

Laura — please proceed with the offer call tomorrow. Use the conditional language in the attached Offer-summary-Julie-Martin.xlsx only if the investor consent is delayed; otherwise finalize and send DocuSign on Dec 15 after consent.

Thanks all — I’ll track investor replies and post the consent outcome.

-Markus
